It was only about a few thousand dollars a night to go on an underwater and moving 'hotel'. But that became possible after we got an email from the NSW Lotteries giving us a few million dollars after we won. The first thing I did was persuade my mum into going on a Sub 2 trip for a few nights, and she, at last, reluctantly agreed to go on a few nights around Australia. Hopes high, I boarded the luxury submarine, and the first thing my family and I did was go to the dining room. We sat on floating recliners and ate pricey food made by a private chef on a floating table the size of a bus. But the highlight of the trip around Australia was the rooms we had booked for rooms for the journey. The door was unlocked by Face ID, and we were greated to a spectacular dining room with an underwater view. As we plonked down onto the hovering king-sized beds, the boat stopped gliding through the ocean like a knife. Assuming that it was normal, we started jumping on the bed. Suddenly, disaster struck, like lightening to a tree. The glass pane that gave us an underwater view cracked like hammer to a rice cracker. Pools of water rushed into the immense room as the waves pushed against us without mercy. We paddled out the window, and for a vertiginous moment, my family and I felt like drowning as we realised we were about a hundred meters below sea level, but the moment left as soon as it had come. I kicked my legs as brutally as I could, one hand paddling and the other clutched onto Mum. At last, I broke free of the nightmare and I was inhaling lungfulls of fresh, salty air, overwhelmed to be at the surface rather than the bottom. But it wasn't over. We were still hundreds of meters away from a sandy shore. I paddled for hours, my thigh and arms screaming at my head in pain. It was Bondi. I was fulled to the brim of joy, and I paddked hard with the strength I suddenly knew I had. I stood like a hero. Raw text: My dreams are somewhat interesting. They used to be normal. The average, everyday ones. Fantasies, school life, nightmares. But when I turned 13, everything changed. I started having more realistic ones, but the funny thing was - they weren't realistic at all. Just last night, I dreamt my house burnt down, my sister and my parents were shrivelled in the fire. A pile of disintagrated ashes. But there was a voice in the background. Always the same one. "You are not who you think you are." It took me about a month to realise that voice was mine. It haunted me - even when I wasn't dreaming. For a while, I just stopped sleeping. You can imagine how that turned out. "Sky!" a voice cuts through my thoughts, clearing my foggy head. "Are you coming to dinner, or what?" "Sorry, mum!" I yell back over my shoulder. "I'll be a sec." Technically, I'm in the attic. However, the attic is so full of family treasures that I discovered, it's more like a safe. The attic makes all these memories and dreams come clear as day. I just don't know why. After dinner, the weird voice starts calling me again. I clamp my hands over my ears, trying to muffle out the screams. My sister, Ruby, looks at me strangely. "Sky, will you stop doing that? That's the third time you've done that this week..." she says huffily, flicking back a strand of blonde hair. "I'm fine! I'm fine. I just..." I sigh. "Why do I look so different from you all?" I finally look at her in the eye, and instantly regret it. Those blue eyes are so cold it's a wonder they don't turn to ice any second. Ruby scoffs. "I don't care. Maybe you were adopted." I stop. Is this it? Is this what I have been looking for? Ruby said it as a joke. Not a particularly funny one - but it was still a joke. All the jigsaw pieces fit pretty perfectly, though. Mum, dad, and Ruby all have blonde hair, pale skin and blue eyes. Meanwhile, I look extremely contrasting with my olive skin, dark eyes, and brown hair streaked with highlights. They're a very tall family as well. I'm avarage in my height, but Ruby was almost a head taller than me when she was my age. And the voice! It all makes sense! "You are not who you think you are" - of course! But then... who are my real parents? "I need to go," I burst out, running to the attic and slamming the splintery wooden door behind me. I sit on the floor, trying to process it. A few times, I think that it is ridiculous. I mean, I only figured this out today. My parentshave to be my ones. The ones I have now. Right? I groan, struggling to make sense of it all. "Where are you? I whispered. "Why did you leave me?" Suddenly, footsteps approach. I scramble to my feet. "Sky?" my dad's voice rings in my ears. "Sky Willows?" I open the door, and sure enough, my parents are there. "I want to know what happened to them." My voice is steady, but my fear underneath it all is unmistakable. "So you finally figured it out," my mum sighs. "Yes. What happened to them?" I ask again. "Oh, don't worry." My dad smiles. Then, as if a light had been shut off, their faces contort into creepy and slightly mad features. "We took care of them."

Eliza took a deep breath, clutching the edge of her seat, looking down on the world. "Roger that, we are ready," said Jim, smiling warmly at Eliza. "Are you ready, Moore?" Eliza looked down at the nametag on her suit.Eliza Moore. "I'm ready, captain." As soon as she said it, the spaceship took off, leaving for Mission Moon. Zoooooom! *** "We are close, Moore," said Jim, adjusting his spacesuit. "We're close to the moon." Eliza smiled as she saw space outside her window. Eliza was scared of space, how it billowed out into nothing, and if you fell in, you'll never make it out of there. Her thoughts were shattered as Jim put a warm hand on her shoulder. "No need to be scared, mate." Eliza smiled, and looked longingly at the refrigerator. She stood up, her legs shaking as she walked over to the refrigerator. She opened the refrigerator door and: BOOM! "Warning, hull damaged," came a glitchy voice from the computer. Eliza shut the door and ran to the side of the spaceship. "We've been hit by some sort of space rock!" shouted Eliza. "What are we going to do, captain?" The spaceship came to a sudden halt as Jim pulled the brakes. "We are still going to the moon, the crew will meet us there," said Jim, controlling the spaceship. "Moore, I need you to go outside and fix the hull." Eliza's mouth hung open. "Me? Captain, I don't what to do." "Yes, you do. You've had the training, mate. Time to get out there and show space what you're made of. Do you hear me?" Eliza nodded. She grabbed the tool kit and opened the side door. Cold air seeped in, and Eliza began to float. She pulled herself to the hull of the ship and got working. After screwing and hammering, the hull was good enough to fly to the moon. It was all Eliza could do for now. She pulled herself back to the ship, shut the door and made her way back to Jim. "I did the best I could, captain. The ship should be able to fly to the moon," said Eliza. Jim started to steer the ship back to it's original course. "Good job, Moore. You have proven that you are worthy to be captain for when I retire." "You're retiring?" asked Eliza sadly. "Not now, but in about 5 years." Eliza smiled. The spaceship stopped and everything shook. "We have landed," Jim spoke into his intercomm on his suit. "We have landed on the moon. Do you copy that H.R.S control centre?" A glitchy voice came back from the comm. "Copy. Congratulations, the Moon Crew are waiting for you." Eliza pulled the door open. She lept out and landed on the moon. Dust swirled everywhere. Moondust. Eliza was on the moon. What an amazing ride.
